resources.string: Your own server (VPS). Hydra signs in over SSH, installs the VPN and maintains it: devices, restart, removal, full cleanup. Sign-in details can be remembered — they are kept encrypted on this device only. The server key fingerprint is pinned, so a substituted server is refused.
No servers yet. You need a VPS with Debian or Ubuntu and root sign-in by password or key.
Use the details from your hosting email: the server address and the root password (or an SSH key). You choose what to install after signing in.
This does not look like a server address
Private SSH key (file text), instead of the password
Remember sign-in (encrypted, on this device only)
This is the server \"fingerprint\" — its unique mark. If your hosting shows it in the panel, compare. From now on Hydra will sign in only to a server with this fingerprint.
The server is in the list below. On its card choose what to install: AmneziaWG (recommended), an OpenFlux node or a panel.
Sign-in not saved — Hydra will ask for the password when needed
The server will be unavailable for 1–2 minutes; the VPN on it starts by itself.

Everything Hydra installed will be removed from %1$s: AmneziaWG, the OpenFlux node, panels, their settings, firewall rules and key copies. Connections to this server in Servers will stop working. Other programs are not touched. The server stays in the list so you can install again.
The record and saved sign-in are removed from the app. Nothing changes on the server itself — to remove the VPN from the server, use \"Wipe server completely\" first.
Not installed. The simplest way to your own VPN — fits most people.
created on another device — its config is there
This device will no longer be able to connect. Others keep working.
One device per phone or computer — you can turn it off without touching the others.
Name in Latin letters, e.g. phone
The service, its settings and programs will be removed from %1$s; port %2$d/udp is closed if Hydra opened it. All devices of this VPN stop connecting.
Not installed. For experienced users: bypasses blocking through services like Yandex Docs.
Channel \"%1$s\", its service and (if no other channels) the node core will be removed. Links to this node stop working.
The node is installed by the official OpenFlux script of a pinned version (SHA-256 verified); the script picks the port. Yandex / Mail.ru transports are optional.
1.0: Jc, Jmin, Jmax, S1, S2, H1–H4. Works with any AmneziaWG client.
1.5: same parameters as 1.0 (signature packets I1–I5 are not set); compatible with 1.0 and 1.5 clients.
2.0: + S3, S4 and H1–H4 ranges. Needs a 2.0+ client (Hydra fits).
3.x: + HeaderProtectionKey, content padding, random trailers. Needs a 3.x client (Hydra fits).
Open the port in the server firewall (ufw/firewalld), if it is on
Done! The connection is added to Servers — pick it and tap Connect.
AmneziaWG settings file. Hydra adds it itself; for the official AmneziaWG app scan the QR or copy the text.
Connection link. Hydra adds it itself; for another app copy it.
This is an access key — do not publish it.
A ready-made website where you create users yourself and hand out links. Handy when several people need the VPN.
Password copied — paste it on the login page
If a 3x-ui panel is already installed on your server, Hydra connects to it and can create users and hand out links. Nothing is installed.
On the server run: x-ui setting -getApiToken (or see XUI_API_TOKEN in /etc/x-ui/install-result.env)
The address starts with http:// - the token travels unencrypted. Connect while the VPN is on (Hydra traffic goes through the tunnel) or use https://.
A user is one person or one device. You will get a connection link.
Not installed. A panel website where you add users and hand out links — handy if several people need the VPN.
A panel not installed by Hydra is already on this server: connect 3x-ui with \"I already have a panel\" (address and token).

The panel, its core and all panel users will be removed from the server. Links issued by the panel stop working. A copy of the panel database (users, settings) stays on the server in /root/hydra-backups.
3x-ui panel connected by token (no server sign-in)
The panel opens over http:// — the site password travels unencrypted. Sign in with the VPN on or set up HTTPS in the panel.
Hydra forgets the panel address and token. The panel and its users do not change.
Panel connected — it is in the list below.

Hydra installs the latest 3x-ui with the official installer, makes up a strong login and password, creates a VLESS + gRPC + Reality connection and the first user, and adds the user\'s subscription to Servers — changes made on the panel site arrive by themselves.
Create users and connections on the panel website; a connection link from the panel can be pasted into Servers.
Hydra installs the latest %1$s with the official installer and sets a strong login, password and a random panel address. You create users on the panel website.
Done! The panel is installed — open it with \"Open panel\" on the server card.
Damaged record: this is how a panel connected in 0.8.1-a looks after being opened in 0.8.0-rc4. Remove it and connect the panel again with \"I already have a panel\".
Disguise (Reality pretends to be this site)
A site from the \"white lists\": the connection still works when a mobile carrier lets only allowed sites through. Downside: a Russian site on a foreign IP is a visible sign for DPI.
A foreign site with no nodes in Russia: the server address does not contradict the disguise. Downside: blocked under mobile \"white lists\".
HTTPS for the panel and subscription: a free Let\'s Encrypt certificate for the server IP (needs port 80/tcp open)
Could not sign in automatically — the password is copied for 30 seconds, paste it into the field
The panel is closed from outside: its website opens only through Hydra, over a secure tunnel to the server.
The panel website will stop opening from the internet: Hydra will open it through a secure connection to the server. Users\' VPN connections keep working as before.
Open the panel to the outside?
The panel website will open from the internet at its address again. It is better to enable HTTPS.
HTTPS for the panel: a free Let\'s Encrypt certificate for the server IP (needs port 80/tcp open; if it fails, the panel stays on HTTP)
Hydra creates it in the panel and adds it to the panel\'s main user: their subscription in Servers picks it up by itself.
Works over UDP: the port will be opened as UDP. Some mobile networks in Russia throttle UDP — then pick VLESS/Trojan + REALITY.
Needs a server certificate: first tap «Enable HTTPS» for the panel.

Hydra installs Docker (if missing), the PasarGuard panel and its node with the official installers of a pinned version and creates the owner with a strong login and password. The panel is reachable only through Hydra\'s secure tunnel. Connections (VLESS / Trojan + REALITY, VMess) — with the “Create connection” button. Takes 3–10 minutes.

Hydra installs Docker (if missing), the Remnawave panel of a pinned version with its database and cache, a small proxy for its website and a node, and creates the owner with a strong login and password. The panel is reachable only through Hydra\'s secure tunnel. Connections (VLESS / Trojan + REALITY) — with the “Create connection” button. Takes 3–10 minutes.
